{
  "title": "Inference-Time Perception Monitoring for VLMs via Complementary Process Reward Distillation",
  "core_problem": "Vision-language models (VLMs) performing multi-step visual mathematical reasoning lack mechanisms for inference-time self-monitoring of perception quality, despite encoding reliable visual evidence in their hidden states. A surge of training-time perception-aware RL methods (MoCA, PEARL, PDCR, PRCO, PeBR, PAPO, VPPO) has dramatically improved VLM perception during training, but NONE provides inference-time step-level monitoring — the model generates better but still cannot detect when a specific step contains a perception error during inference. External multimodal PRMs (URSA, Perceval, VL-PRM) provide effective inference-time monitoring but double compute cost. Can we distill multimodal PRM perception-error expertise into a near-zero-cost auxiliary monitoring head that complements training-time perception RL, giving VLMs both improved perception AND the ability to catch residual errors at inference time?",
  "opportunity": "A critical gap exists between training-time and inference-time perception improvements for VLMs. Training-time methods (MoCA's modality-aware credit assignment, PEARL's perception checklists, PDCR's decomposed confidence rewards, PRCO's Observer/Solver coevolution, PeBR's two-stage RL, PAPO's implicit perception loss, VPPO's trajectory advantage shaping) have collectively demonstrated that decomposing perception from reasoning during RL training yields substantial gains (+5-10% on MathVista/MathVerse). However, ALL these methods operate exclusively at training time — they produce better-trained models but provide no mechanism for inference-time step-level monitoring. When a perception-RL-trained model encounters a novel visual pattern at inference time and misreads a diagram, there is no internal signal to detect or correct the error. Meanwhile, 'Seeing but Not Believing' (arXiv 2510.17771) reveals that VLM hidden states DO encode reliable visual evidence in deep layers — probes achieve >92% accuracy at flagging unreliable responses (arXiv 2508.18297) — but VLMs under-utilize this signal during generation. This creates a precise technical opportunity: the hidden-state signal EXISTS but is not LEVERAGED for step-level monitoring. A trained auxiliary head can bridge this utilization gap. Separately, a rich ecosystem of multimodal PRMs (URSA-RM, Perceval, Athena-PRM, VL-PRM, MM-PRM) encodes curated perception-error expertise from hundreds of thousands of step-level annotations — URSA's 302K misinterpretation-insertion examples, Perceval's perception-centric token-level grounding — representing error patterns that outcome-based RL exploration is unlikely to discover independently. The practical opportunity: distill this PRM expertise into a lightweight auxiliary head that (a) reads the hidden-state perception signals VLMs already encode but don't use, (b) provides near-zero-cost inference-time step monitoring that no training-time perception RL method offers, and (c) is demonstrably complementary to training-time perception RL, yielding gains beyond either approach alone.",
  "landscape": "**Training-Time Perception-Aware RL (the crowded frontier — all training-only, no inference monitoring):** 'Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking?' / MoCA (arXiv 2605.14054, ICML 2026 Spotlight) introduces Modality-Aware Credit Assignment routing rewards to perception vs. reasoning via a blindfolded reasoning proxy (Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B), achieving 73.8 MathVista on Qwen2.5-VL-7B without any PRM. PEARL (arXiv 2511.18437, CVPR 2026) uses dual-branch perception checklists with rule-based verification, +9.7% on MathVerse, +5.6 average over GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-7B. PDCR (arXiv 2605.13467, May 2026) decomposes confidence rewards via intra-cluster normalization for perception vs. reasoning tokens. PRCO (arXiv 2603.28618, Mar 2026) coevolves Observer (evidence caption) and Solver roles within a shared policy, +7pt average over base. 'From Seeing to Thinking' (arXiv 2605.20177, May 2026) demonstrates staged perception-then-reasoning training, showing perception is better learned via RL than SFT, +5.2% WeMath. PAPO (arXiv 2507.06448, ICLR 2026) adds implicit perception loss maximizing KL on original vs. corrupted images, 30.5% perception error reduction. VPPO (arXiv 2510.09285, ICLR 2026) reshapes advantages via visual dependency, achieving SOTA at 8B scale. PeBR (arXiv 2509.13031, Sep 2025) pioneers two-stage perception-first then reasoning RL. Perception-R1 (arXiv 2506.07218, Jun 2025) uses visual perception reward via LLM-judged consistency, SOTA with only 1442 examples. Difference Feedback (arXiv 2603.27482, Mar 2026) generates process-level masks via trajectory repair for VLM GRPO. SPARC (arXiv 2602.06566, Feb 2026) separates perception/reasoning circuits at inference but for test-time compute scaling, not step monitoring. KEY OBSERVATION: None of these methods provides a trained internal mechanism for detecting step-level perception errors at inference time. **VLM Hidden-State Perception Encoding (the overlooked signal):** 'Seeing but Not Believing' (arXiv 2510.17771, Oct 2025) demonstrates VLMs encode reliable visual evidence in deep layers but under-utilize it — the issue is utilization, not absence. Probes on VLM internal states achieve >92% accuracy at flagging unreliable responses (arXiv 2508.18297). 'Reasoning Models Know When They're Right' (arXiv 2504.05419) shows step correctness is linearly encoded in LLM hidden states (AUC 0.80-0.91). ReProbe (arXiv 2511.06209) trains <10M param probes matching 7B PRMs. This evidence supports our auxiliary head approach — the signal is there, waiting to be extracted. **External Multimodal PRMs (teacher candidates with curated error expertise):** URSA-RM-8B (NeurIPS 2025) trained on DualMath-1.1M including 302K misinterpretation-insertion examples, uses SAM-B+SigLIP-L hybrid vision tower with Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct backbone, encoding systematic perception error patterns. Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, Apr 2026) provides token-level perception-centric error grounding on Qwen-VL family — the closest architecture match for our Qwen3-VL policy. Athena-PRM (arXiv 2506.09532) achieves SOTA on VisualProcessBench with only 5K training samples. VL-PRM (arXiv 2509.23250) shows smaller VL-PRMs match larger ones, and perception-focused supervision boosts test-time scaling. MM-PRM (arXiv 2505.13427) provides 700K+ MCTS-based step annotations. **VLM Self-Verification (documented limitations):** 'Aha Moment Revisited' (arXiv 2506.17417) shows VLM self-verification strategies consistently underperform majority voting. Sherlock (arXiv 2505.22651) finds self-correction activates in <10% of samples. These failures motivate the need for a TRAINED monitoring head rather than prompting-based self-verification. **Multi-Role VLM Architectures (related but distinct):** ADPO (arXiv 2601.01483) jointly trains generation and outcome-level verification (+2.8% MathVista, -53.5% FLOPs) — outcome-level only, no process monitoring. PRCO's Observer/Solver shares parameters but requires full generation passes for each role. Agent0-VL (arXiv 2511.19900) uses Solver/Verifier with tool integration. Critic-V (CVPR 2025) trains a separate VLM critic via DPO. MM-Verify (ACL 2025) uses chain-of-thought verification with separate verifier. VALOR (ICLR 2026) uses annotation-free verifiers for spatial reasoning. 'Journey Before Destination' (arXiv 2512.12218) decomposes chains into perception vs. reasoning steps with off-the-shelf VLM judges for faithfulness — a training-free inference method but requires full VLM judge passes. VisVM (arXiv 2412.03704, ICCV 2025) trains a vision value model for caption search via temporal difference learning. All either use FULL model forward passes for verification (expensive) or operate on text output only (missing perception signals from hidden states). **Our key differentiator:** We occupy a unique position at the intersection of two orthogonal axes: (1) SIGNAL SOURCE — we distill from trained multimodal PRMs that encode curated perception-error expertise, unlike training-time RL methods that discover perception patterns through exploration alone; (2) DEPLOYMENT — we internalize monitoring into a near-zero-cost auxiliary head on hidden states, unlike all external PRMs, multi-role architectures requiring full generation passes, and text-only probes missing visual features. The closest comparisons are: Perceval (uses perception-centric PRM but keeps it external), ADPO (internalizes verification but outcome-level only), ReProbe/STEP (lightweight probes but text-only), and 'Journey Before Destination' (inference-time perception checking but training-free with full VLM judge passes). No existing work distills multimodal process-level perception-error expertise into a near-zero-cost inference-time monitoring head.",

  "approach": "Architecture: Perception-Aware Monitoring Head (PAMH). Augment a Qwen3-VL-8B policy with a lightweight auxiliary monitoring head — a 2-layer MLP (hidden dim 256, ReLU) plus linear classification layer — atop the shared vision-language transformer backbone. Unlike PRCO's Observer (requires full generation pass) or Critic-V (separate DPO-trained VLM), PAMH reads from the EXISTING hidden states at step boundaries, contributing negligible marginal compute (<0.1% of a forward pass). The head predicts decomposed step-quality scores: P(perception_error | h_t) and P(reasoning_error | h_t), providing error-type-specific monitoring motivated by MoCA's insight that perception and reasoning errors require different interventions.\n\nTraining Pipeline (4 phases):\n\nPhase 0 — Perception-Aware RL Base (modular, optional). Apply perception-aware RL training to Qwen3-VL-8B following the PEARL paradigm: construct perception checklists for training problems, use dual-branch GRPO with perception rewards (lambda=0.1). This establishes a strong base model with improved perception, serving as the foundation for PRM distillation. We test both with and without this phase to quantify complementarity.\n\nPhase 1 — PRM Trajectory Scoring & Signal Extraction. Sample ~50K multimodal math reasoning trajectories from the (optionally perception-RL-trained) Qwen3-VL-8B policy across MathV360K, GeoQA, and MMathCoT problems. Score with multiple teacher PRMs to address the cross-architecture concern: (a) Perceval (primary teacher — built on Qwen-VL family, providing architectural compatibility and perception-centric token-level error grounding), (b) URSA-RM-8B (complementary teacher — SAM-B+SigLIP-L+Qwen2.5-Math architecture, providing curated misinterpretation expertise from 302K insertion examples). Extract two types of step-level signals: (i) drop-moment indicators where PRM detects relative score decreases between consecutive steps, and (ii) perception-specific error flags from Perceval's token-level grounding identifying which errors stem from visual misinterpretation vs. reasoning failures. Validate cross-architecture scoring quality via human annotation on a 500-sample subset, measuring inter-PRM agreement and error-type classification accuracy.\n\nPhase 2 — PAMH Training with Complementary Signals. Three-stage curriculum: (2a) Warm-up: freeze VLM backbone, train only PAMH on PRM-labeled trajectories with binary cross-entropy for both perception-error and reasoning-error detection heads, using 'Seeing but Not Believing'-motivated layer selection (deep layers 20+ where perception evidence is most concentrated). (2b) Joint fine-tuning: unfreeze backbone with gradient scaling (lambda=0.1-0.3) on PAMH loss, KL regularization (beta=0.01) against original policy to prevent catastrophic forgetting — especially critical for preserving the perception improvements from Phase 0. (2c) Perception-error curriculum: oversample trajectories where Perceval identifies visual misinterpretation steps, weighted 3x, targeting the specific error class that training-time RL is least likely to have fully addressed.\n\nPhase 3 — Inference-Time Monitoring Protocol. During generation, PAMH provides step-quality estimates at each step boundary. When P(perception_error) exceeds a calibrated threshold tau_p, trigger image re-examination with an explicit perception verification prompt (inspired by MoCA's structured verbal verification). When P(reasoning_error) exceeds tau_r, trigger standard backtracking and re-generation. Thresholds are calibrated on a held-out validation set to optimize the precision-recall tradeoff, targeting >80% precision to avoid unnecessary backtracking.\n\nEvaluation Design — Systematic Comparison Across Both Axes.\n\nBenchmarks: MathVista (overall + GPS subset), MathVerse (testmini, 6 input variants including vision-only), MathVision, GeoQA, WE-MATH, VisualProcessBench.\n\nBaseline organization along two axes:\n(A) Training-time perception methods (no inference monitoring): PEARL (CVPR 2026), MoCA (ICML 2026), PDCR, PAPO (ICLR 2026), VPPO (ICLR 2026), vanilla GRPO. We use published numbers where available on matched model scales and reproduce 2-3 key methods on Qwen3-VL-8B.\n(B) Inference-time monitoring methods: external PRM (Perceval, URSA-RM), majority voting (documented strong baseline), vanilla self-verification, ADPO, VisVM-guided search.\n(C) Combined systems (our contribution): (C1) PAMH-only (no perception RL base), (C2) Perception-RL-only (PEARL-style, no PAMH), (C3) PAMH + perception RL (full method), (C4) Frozen probe baseline (ReProbe-style adapted to multimodal), (C5) VeriThinker-style verification fine-tuning adapted to multimodal.\n\nKey ablations: (i) Perceval-only vs. URSA-only vs. multi-teacher signal; (ii) deep-layer-only vs. all-layer hidden state input to PAMH; (iii) decomposed (perception+reasoning) vs. unified error detection; (iv) perception-error curriculum weight; (v) Phase 0 with vs. without perception RL base; (vi) PAMH architecture (linear vs. 2-layer MLP vs. 3-layer).\n\nPrimary hypotheses: (H1) PAMH achieves at least 90% of external PRM-guided accuracy at <5% of PRM inference FLOPs; (H2) PAMH + perception RL base outperforms either alone by at least 2% on perception-heavy subsets (MathVista-GPS, MathVerse vision-only); (H3) Perceval's perception-centric signals yield better PAMH calibration than URSA's more general drop-moments for perception errors specifically; (H4) Deep-layer hidden states (layers 20+) provide significantly better perception-error detection, consistent with 'Seeing but Not Believing'.",

## Reviewer feedback (round 3)
Issues: ["CRITICAL: Missing 10+ directly relevant references in VLM hidden-state probing for error detection. Most threatening: (1) HALP (EACL 2026, arXiv 2603.05465) trains lightweight probes on VLM hidden states achieving 0.93 AUROC for hallucination detection pre-generation — essentially the same technical approach as PAMH but without PRM distillation; (2) VIB-Probe (arXiv 2601.05547, Jan 2026) uses variational information bottleneck on VLM attention heads for inference-time hallucination mitigation; (3) EnsemHalDet (arXiv 2604.02784, Apr 2026) trains ensemble of internal state detectors on VLM hidden states and attention; (4) 'Reading Between the Lines' (arXiv 2511.19806) trains latent representation probes on VLM hidden states for OCR perception error detection — directly comparable.", "CRITICAL: Missing 'Don't Blink: Evidence Collapse during Multimodal Reasoning' (arXiv 2604.04207, Apr 2026) which directly demonstrates the phenomenon PAMH aims to detect — VLMs losing visual grounding during multi-step reasoning — and proposes its own 'vision veto' intervention mechanism. This is a must-cite paper that could either support or threaten the PAMH approach.", "SIGNIFICANT: Perceval ALREADY provides both training-time AND inference-time perception monitoring with token-level error grounding. The proposal correctly identifies Perceval as 'external' but undersells its inference-time capabilities. PAMH's value proposition reduces to 'approximate Perceval at lower cost' — an efficiency argument, not a capability gap. The claimed 'training-time vs. inference-time gap' is already partially closed by Perceval itself.", "SIGNIFICANT: Missing LaSeR (arXiv 2510.14943, Oct 2025) which trains a last-token self-rewarding auxiliary mechanism on hidden states for near-zero-cost verification; Gnosis (arXiv 2512.20578, Dec 2025) which trains ~5M parameter self-awareness heads on hidden states for correctness prediction; and Octopus-8B (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.08503) which achieves SOTA VLM self-correction. All represent approaches to internalizing verification signals.", "NOVELTY JUSTIFICATION GAP: The proposal does not address why PRM-distilled probes should outperform directly-trained probes (HALP-style). If lightweight probes can achieve 0.93 AUROC by training directly on error labels, what additional value does the PRM distillation intermediate step provide? The argument that PRM distillation captures richer step-level process signals beyond binary outcome labels needs to be made explicit and tested as an ablation.", "Missing additional works: VisualPRM (arXiv 2503.10291) — its VisualProcessBench is used but the model is not cited; 'Grounding the Score'/EVPV (arXiv 2603.16253) — lightweight visual premise verification for VLM PRMs; PROPA (arXiv 2511.10279) — process-level optimization via MCTS+GRPO; G1 (arXiv 2505.13426) — perception-reasoning bootstrapping; REVERSE (arXiv 2504.13169) — unified hallucination-aware training with on-the-fly self-verification; 'Anatomy of a Lie'/CAD (arXiv 2603.15557) — cognitive anomaly detection using information-theoretic probes on VLM generation trajectories.", "The '<0.1% marginal inference cost' claim is misleading. While the MLP forward pass may be negligible, the actual inference-time cost includes the re-examination/backtracking triggered when perception errors are detected. With regeneration from verified prefixes (similar to Perceval's truncation-regeneration), the total cost increase is substantially higher and depends on the false positive rate of the monitor.", "ICLR 2027 and CVPR 2027 deadlines are NOT officially announced — they are projected from historical patterns. While this is acknowledged in the proposal, the primary target relies on an unconfirmed deadline."]
Feedback: The Round 2→3 revision shows excellent improvement: comprehensive training-time perception RL landscape, well-structured evaluation, clear complementarity framing. However, a critical blind spot has emerged: the VLM hidden-state probing landscape is far more developed than the proposal acknowledges. Required revisions:

1. **Add ALL missing VLM probing references** (HALP, VIB-Probe, EnsemHalDet, 'Reading Between the Lines', 'Don't Blink', LaSeR, Gnosis, Octopus, REVERSE, 'Anatomy of a Lie', VisualPRM, EVPV). Position HALP as the most direct baseline — it achieves 0.93 AUROC by probing VLM hidden states for hallucination detection WITHOUT PRM distillation.

2. **Add HALP-style direct probing as an explicit ablation/baseline** (call it C6). This baseline trains the same lightweight MLP on ground-truth perception error labels rather than PRM-distilled signals. The comparison between C3 (PAMH with PRM distillation) and C6 (direct-probe baseline) is essential to justify the PRM distillation step.

## Paper 1: VisualPRM (arXiv 2503.10291)

**Title:** "VisualPRM: An Effective Process Reward Model for Multimodal Reasoning"

**Authors:** Weiyun Wang, Zhangwei Gao, Lianjie Chen, Zhe Chen, Jinguo Zhu, Xiangyu Zhao, Yangzhou Liu, Yue Cao, Shenglong Ye, Xizhou Zhu, Lewei Lu, Haodong Duan, Yu Qiao, Jifeng Dai, Wenhai Wang

**Submitted:** March 13, 2025

**Key Approach:** An 8B-parameter multimodal Process Reward Model that scores intermediate reasoning steps of VLMs. It is trained on VisualPRM400K, a process-supervision dataset built through an automated annotation pipeline. At inference time, it uses Best-of-N (BoN) evaluation -- generating N candidate solutions and selecting the one with the highest process reward score.

**Main Results:** Achieves a 5.9-point average improvement across seven multimodal reasoning benchmarks when applied to InternVL2.5-78B. Demonstrates gains across different MLLM families and scales, and outperforms outcome-based reward models.

**Key Contributions:**
- **VisualPRM400K:** Large-scale automated process-supervision dataset
- **VisualProcessBench:** A human-annotated benchmark with step-wise correctness labels that measures a PRM's ability to detect erroneous steps in multimodal reasoning

**Relevance to the proposal:** This is directly foundational. The proposal already uses VisualProcessBench as an evaluation benchmark but fails to cite the VisualPRM model itself. VisualPRM is the leading VLM-specific PRM and the most direct prior work for any proposal building process reward models for multimodal reasoning. It must be cited both as (c) a process reward model for VLMs and (a) a method for detecting reasoning errors at the step level.

---

## Paper 2: "Grounding the Score" / EVPV (arXiv 2603.16253)

**Title:** "Grounding the Score: Explicit Visual Premise Verification for Reliable Vision-Language Process Reward Models"

**Authors:** Junxin Wang, Dai Guan, Weijie Qiu, Zhihang Li, Yongbo Gai, Zhengyi Yang, Mengyu Zhou, Erchao Zhao, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

**Submitted:** March 17, 2026 (revised May 9, 2026)

**Key Approach:** Introduces Explicit Visual Premise Verification (EVPV), a lightweight verification interface that decouples perceptual errors from reasoning errors in VLM PRMs. The mechanism works in three stages:
1. **Step-wise Visual Checklist:** The policy model produces an explicit checklist of visual facts required by each reasoning step.
2. **Constraint Extraction:** A constraint extractor independently derives structured visual constraints from the input image.
3. **Reliability Gating:** Checklist claims are matched against extracted constraints to compute a scalar visual reliability signal. PRM step rewards are attenuated when visual reliability is low, preserved when high.

This decouples perceptual uncertainty from logical evaluation without requiring per-step tool calls.

**Main Results:** Improves step-level verification on VisualProcessBench and consistently boosts Best-of-N reranking accuracy across six multimodal reasoning benchmarks (LogicVista, MMMU, MathVerse-VO, MathVision, MathVista, WeMath). Controlled constraint corruption experiments show monotonic performance degradation, providing causal evidence that gains come from constraint fidelity.

**Relevance to the proposal:** This is highly relevant to all three themes. It directly addresses (a) VLM perception error detection by separating visual misperception from reasoning errors; (b) internalized verification by building explicit visual checklists into the generation process; and (c) process reward models by calibrating PRM scores based on perceptual reliability. If the proposal's core thesis involves making PRMs aware of perception errors, EVPV is the most direct competing/complementary approach.

---

## Paper 3: PROPA (arXiv 2511.10279)

**Title:** "PROPA: Toward Process-level Optimization in Visual Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning"

**Authors:** Yanbei Jiang, Chao Lei, Yihao Ding, Krista Ehinger, Jey Han Lau

**Submitted:** November 13, 2025

**Key Approach:** Integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to provide process-level (step-by-step) rewards for VLM training without requiring expensive human annotations. Key design choices:
- MCTS generates intermediate reward signals by exploring reasoning trajectories
- Training interleaves GRPO updates with SFT, enabling the model to learn from both successful and failed reasoning paths
- A Process Reward Model guides inference-time tree search

**Main Results:** Achieves up to 17.0% gains on in-domain tasks and 21.0% gains on out-of-domain tasks across seven benchmarks and four VLM variants, demonstrating strong generalization.

**Relevance to the proposal:** Directly relevant to (c) process reward models for VLMs. PROPA demonstrates that MCTS-based trajectory exploration can generate reliable process-level supervision for VLM reasoning without human annotation -- a key practical challenge. If the proposal involves training PRMs or using RL for VLM reasoning improvement, PROPA is an important baseline and methodological reference.

---

## Paper 4: G1 (arXiv 2505.13426)

**Title:** "G1: Bootstrapping Perception and Reasoning Abilities of Vision-Language Model via Reinforcement Learning"

**Authors:** Liang Chen, Hongcheng Gao, Tianyu Liu, Zhiqi Huang, Flood Sung, Xinyu Zhou, Yuxin Wu, Baobao Chang

**Submitted:** May 19, 2025

**Key Approach:** Addresses the "knowing-doing gap" -- VLMs perform well on static benchmarks but struggle in interactive visual environments. Introduces VLM-Gym, an RL environment with diverse visual games for scalable multi-game training. Two model variants:
- **G0:** Pure RL-driven self-evolution (no supervised data)
- **G1:** Perception-enhanced initialization before RL fine-tuning

The central finding is that perception and reasoning abilities mutually bootstrap each other during RL training -- improving perception improves reasoning, which in turn demands better perception.

**Main Results:** G1 models consistently exceed their teacher model's performance across all tested games and outperform proprietary models including Claude-3.7-Sonnet-Thinking.

**Relevance to the proposal:** Primarily relevant to (a) perception error detection and (b) internalized verification. G1 demonstrates that perception and reasoning are deeply coupled in VLMs and that RL can jointly improve both. The "mutual bootstrapping" finding is important context for any proposal that treats perception verification as a separable module -- G1 suggests these capabilities are intertwined and can be co-trained.

---

## Paper 5: REVERSE (arXiv 2504.13169)

**Title:** "Generate, but Verify: Reducing Hallucination in Vision-Language Models with Retrospective Resampling"

**Authors:** Tsung-Han Wu, Heekyung Lee, Jiaxin Ge, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Trevor Darrell, David M. Chan

**Submitted:** April 17, 2025 (accepted to NeurIPS 2025)

**Key Approach:** A unified framework combining hallucination-aware training with on-the-fly self-verification during inference:
- **Training:** Uses a dataset of 1.3M+ semi-synthetic samples designed to teach the model to recognize hallucinated content
- **Inference:** Employs "retrospective resampling" -- during generation, the model detects hallucinations and dynamically revises them in real time

**Main Results:** Achieves state-of-the-art hallucination reduction, improving by up to 12% on CHAIR-MSCOCO and 34% on HaloQuest compared to existing approaches.

**Relevance to the proposal:** Strongly relevant to (b) internalized verification. REVERSE demonstrates that VLMs can be trained to detect and correct their own hallucinations during generation -- this is exactly the "self-verification" capability that a proposal on internalized verification would need to position against. The retrospective resampling mechanism is a concrete example of inference-time self-correction without external tools. Also relevant to (a) perception error detection since visual hallucinations are a core type of perception error.

---

## Paper 6: "Anatomy of a Lie" / CAD (arXiv 2603.15557)

**Title:** "Anatomy of a Lie: A Multi-Stage Diagnostic Framework for Tracing Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models"

**Authors:** Lexiang Xiong, Qi Li, Jingwen Ye, Xinchao Wang

**Submitted:** March 16, 2026

**Key Approach:** Recasts hallucinations from static output errors into dynamic pathologies of a model's computational cognition. The framework:
1. **Information-Theoretic Probes:** Project a VLM's generation trajectory onto a low-dimensional "Cognitive State Space"
2. **Geometric-Information Duality:** The central discovery -- a trajectory's geometric abnormality in Cognitive State Space is fundamentally equivalent to its information-theoretic surprisal
3. **Hallucination as Geometric Anomaly:** Detection reduces to anomaly detection in the Cognitive State Space
4. **Three Pathological States:** Maps errors to (i) perceptual instability (Perceptual Entropy), (ii) logical-causal failure (Inferential Conflict), and (iii) decisional ambiguity (Decision Entropy)

**Main Results:** State-of-the-art across POPE (binary QA), MME (comprehensive reasoning), and MS-COCO (open-ended captioning). Operates effectively under weak supervision and remains robust even with heavily contaminated calibration data.

**Relevance to the proposal:** Deeply relevant to (a) VLM perception error detection and (b) internalized verification. CAD provides an interpretable, mechanistic framework for understanding *why* VLMs hallucinate by tracing the internal computational trajectory. The decomposition into perceptual instability vs. logical failure vs. decisional ambiguity directly aligns with any proposal that distinguishes perception errors from reasoning errors. The information-theoretic probe approach could complement or compete with process reward model approaches by offering a white-box diagnostic rather than a learned scoring function.

---

## Summary of Gap Analysis

| Paper | Most Relevant Theme | Why It Must Be Cited |
|-------|-------------------|---------------------|
| VisualPRM | (c) VLM PRMs | Origin of VisualProcessBench; leading VLM PRM baseline |
| EVPV | (a)+(c) Perception + PRMs | Directly decouples perception errors from reasoning in PRMs |
| PROPA | (c) VLM PRMs | MCTS+GRPO for annotation-free process-level VLM training |
| G1 | (a)+(b) Perception + Verification | Shows perception-reasoning mutual bootstrapping via RL |
| REVERSE | (b) Internalized verification | On-the-fly self-verification during VLM generation |
| CAD | (a)+(b) Perception + Verification | Information-theoretic hallucination tracing with interpretable pathological states |

The two most critical omissions for a VLM PRM proposal are **VisualPRM** (since the proposal already uses its benchmark) and **EVPV** (since it directly addresses perception-reasoning disentanglement in VLM PRMs, which appears to be the proposal's core contribution space).

## Paper 1: "Don't Blink: Evidence Collapse during Multimodal Reasoning" (arXiv 2604.04207, April 2026)

**Authors:** Suresh Raghu and Satwik Pandey  
**Venue:** Submitted to UAI 2026  
**Code:** https://github.com/R-Suresh07/Dont-Blink

### What is "Evidence Collapse"?

Evidence collapse is a phenomenon where VLMs progressively lose visual grounding during multi-step reasoning, even as they become more accurate in their final answers. Specifically:

- **Quantification:** Measured via attention weights to annotated evidence regions (bounding boxes) across reasoning positions. Two metrics are used:
  - **Total visual attention mass (V_t):** Aggregated attention across grounding layers to all visual tokens
  - **Evidence attention mass (A_bbox,t):** Restricted to tokens overlapping manually-annotated bounding boxes
  - **Decay formula:** Delta_A_bbox = A_bbox,Start - A_bbox,AnsEnd

- **Severity:** Relative loss ranges from 53.3% (Qwen3-VL-2B on HallusionBench) to 90.8% (GLM on HallusionBench). Over half the evidence attention mass is lost as reasoning unfolds.

- **Sampling positions:** Five reasoning positions (Start, Early/40%, Mid/60%, Late/80%, EndThink) plus answer positions (AnsStart, AnsEnd). Peak discrimination occurs during the reasoning phase in 7/9 model-dataset cells. Endpoint-only measurement misses up to 77.5% of signal.

### The "Vision Veto" Mechanism

A two-stage selective prediction policy:

1. Apply entropy-only deferral at target coverage (e.g., 90%)
2. Among accepted samples, **veto the bottom 5% by cumulative visual engagement**
3. Re-loosen entropy threshold to restore target coverage

This is driven by an **entropy-vision interaction model** (logistic regression):
```
logit(p(correct)) = beta_0 + beta_e * Ez + beta_v * Vz + beta_ev * (Ez * Vz) + beta_l * Lz
```
Where beta_ev < 0 indicates the "confident-but-blind penalty" -- samples that are confident (low entropy) AND visually disengaged are dangerous.

**Task-conditional application:** The veto is only applied on tasks where beta_ev is significantly negative (sustained visual-reference tasks like MMMU_Pro expert STEM questions). On symbolic tasks like MathVista, disengagement is expected and benign.

- **Datasets:** MathVista, HallusionBench, MMMU_Pro (300 samples each with manual bounding boxes; 2,700 total model-example runs)
- **Models tested:** Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, GLM-4.6V-Flash

- Vision veto reduces selective risk by **up to 1.9 percentage points at 90% coverage** on MMMU_Pro
- "Confident-but-blind" quadrant has **15-40 percentage points higher error rate** than grounded predictions on high-risk tasks
- Full-generation entropy is the strongest text-only uncertainty metric (Cohen's d up to -0.90)
- Naive linear fusion of entropy + vision features often hurts transfer performance

### Relevance to Monitoring Perception Quality Per Reasoning Step

This paper directly argues that:
- Text-only monitoring (entropy, confidence) **cannot detect visual disengagement**
- Monitoring must extract cumulative attention metrics across reasoning positions (trapezoidal area under the V-trajectory during thinking)

   - **Negative:** correct-to-wrong, wrong-to-wrong

- **Stage I:** o1 is treated as fixed context. Loss is masked for all tokens in the initial response; policy updates only from o2. A KL penalty constrains o1's distribution. Reward weighting: 90% shaped reward (self-correction) / 10% format reward.

- **Stage II:** Selectively unmasks o1 but only for consistent-correctness samples (correct-to-correct or wrong-to-wrong) to prevent conflicting gradients.

|-----------|-----------------|

| MathVerse | 68.5% |
| WeMath | 84.0% |
| HallusionBench | 64.2% |
| MMStar | 75.2% |

- Multi-pass approaches requiring additional model calls

- Separate verifier models

## Deep Analysis of Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, April 2026)

### 1. Training-Time AND Inference-Time Capabilities

**Yes, Perceval provides BOTH:**

**Training-time (RL integration):**
- Perceval identifies hallucinated token spans in model responses during GRPO-based RL training
- It constructs a binary mask `M_i` where `m_{i,t} = 1` for hallucinated tokens
- Token-level advantages are modulated: `A'_{i,t} := A_i - alpha * m_{i,t} * |A_i|` (where alpha controls penalty strength)
- This replaces the coarse sequence-level advantage of standard GRPO with fine-grained per-token credit assignment
- Perceval is only applied on perception-related data; for math reasoning data, standard GRPO is used unmodified

**Inference-time (test-time scaling):**
- Perceval monitors generations in real-time, detecting perceptual hallucinations
- Two iterative strategies (up to k iterations):
  - **Truncate-then-Regenerate**: Truncate before the first hallucinated span, preserve verified prefix, resample continuation
  - **Truncate-Thinking-then-Regenerate**: Same truncation, but appends a reflection prompt (e.g., "Wait, I need to reconsider... the mug is NOT on the brick") before regeneration

---

### 2. Inference-Time Capabilities in Detail

**Token-level error grounding:**
- Perceval uses a think-then-answer paradigm (`<think>...</think>` and `<answer>...</answer>` tags)
- It extracts image-related claims from the VLM's response and compares each against visual evidence
- Output is a Python list of exact error strings from the response
- Exact string matching locates the token span `[j_k, l_k]` in the original response

**Truncation-regeneration loop:**
- Iterates up to k times (experiments use k=4, 8, 16)
- Terminates when no new errors are flagged or max iterations reached
- At k=16, the Truncate strategy on a 3B model achieves:
  - V* All: 89.53 (vs. 85.86 for majority voting)
  - V* Attr: 94.78 (vs. 92.17)
  - V* Pos: 81.57 (vs. 76.32)

---

### 3. Computational Cost at Inference Time

**Critical finding: The paper provides NO explicit computational cost analysis.** This is a significant gap.

Implicit cost indicators:
- Each iteration requires a full forward pass of Perceval (same size as policy: 3B or 7B) to detect errors
- Each iteration also requires regeneration by the policy model from the truncation point
- With k=16 iterations, worst case = 16 Perceval calls + 16 partial regenerations
- The authors note they "trade a bit more compute for stronger factual grounding" but never quantify this

**Estimated overhead (inferred):**
- Perceval is the same architecture/size as the policy model (Qwen2.5-VL 3B or 7B)
- Each verification step = ~1 full forward pass of an equivalent-size model
- For k iterations: overhead is approximately k * (cost of one PRM pass + cost of partial regeneration)
- This is substantially more expensive than majority voting (which only requires N independent generations)

No latency numbers, throughput benchmarks, or wall-clock comparisons are provided anywhere in the paper or in follow-up discussions found online.

---

### 4. Comparison to Lightweight Probe/MLP on Hidden States

**Perceval does NOT compare against probe-based approaches.** However, I found highly relevant work:

**HALP (arXiv 2603.05465, March 2026)** detects hallucinations in VLMs using hidden state probes:
- Architecture: 3-layer MLP (512 -> 256 -> 128 dimensions)
- Inference time: **10-15ms** per sample (vs. full model forward pass for Perceval)
- Overhead: **<1%** relative to full generation
- AUROC: ~0.89 average on query token representations
- Operates **pre-generation** (single forward pass, no decoding needed)

**Key differences:**
| Aspect | Perceval | HALP-style Probe |
|--------|----------|-----------------|
| Parameters | 3B-7B (full VLM) | ~200K (tiny MLP) |
| Inference cost | Full forward pass per check | 10-15ms per sample |
| Granularity | Token-span error grounding with explanations | Binary hallucination probability |
| Actionability | Can truncate and guide regeneration | Can only flag risk pre-generation |
| Training data | Requires carefully curated perception-centric annotations | Trained on hidden states from existing data |

The fundamental trade-off: Perceval is orders of magnitude more expensive but provides actionable, fine-grained error localization that enables the truncation-regeneration loop. Probes are nearly free but only provide a binary signal.

---

### 5. Benchmarks and Results

**Perceval's results (Qwen2.5-VL backbone):**

|-----------|---------|-------------|---------|-------------|
| V* All | 80.10 | **83.25** | 84.29 | **86.39** |
| V* Attr | 86.95 | **90.43** | 85.22 | **86.09** |
| V* Pos | 69.73 | **72.37** | 82.89 | **86.84** |
| BLINK | 49.13 | 48.75 | 53.55 | **54.49** |
| MMStar | 55.3 | **55.8** | 62.0 | **63.8** |
| MathVision | 23.36 | **26.32** | 27.96 | **30.92** |

| ChartQA | 83.32 | **86.48** | 85.16 | 84.44 |
| RealWorldQA | 62.1 | **64.9** | 66.4 | **67.4** |

|--------|--------|-------|

## Deep Analysis of Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, April 2026)

### 1. Training-Time AND Inference-Time Capabilities

**Yes, Perceval provides BOTH:**

**Training-time (RL integration):**
- Perceval identifies hallucinated token spans in model responses during GRPO-based RL training
- It constructs a binary mask `M_i` where `m_{i,t} = 1` for hallucinated tokens
- Token-level advantages are modulated: `A'_{i,t} := A_i - alpha * m_{i,t} * |A_i|` (where alpha controls penalty strength)
- This replaces the coarse sequence-level advantage of standard GRPO with fine-grained per-token credit assignment
- Perceval is only applied on perception-related data; for math reasoning data, standard GRPO is used unmodified

**Inference-time (test-time scaling):**
- Perceval monitors generations in real-time, detecting perceptual hallucinations
- Two iterative strategies (up to k iterations):
  - **Truncate-then-Regenerate**: Truncate before the first hallucinated span, preserve verified prefix, resample continuation
  - **Truncate-Thinking-then-Regenerate**: Same truncation, but appends a reflection prompt (e.g., "Wait, I need to reconsider... the mug is NOT on the brick") before regeneration

---

### 2. Inference-Time Capabilities in Detail

**Token-level error grounding:**
- Perceval uses a think-then-answer paradigm (`<think>...</think>` and `<answer>...</answer>` tags)
- It extracts image-related claims from the VLM's response and compares each against visual evidence
- Output is a Python list of exact error strings from the response
- Exact string matching locates the token span `[j_k, l_k]` in the original response

**Truncation-regeneration loop:**
- Iterates up to k times (experiments use k=4, 8, 16)
- Terminates when no new errors are flagged or max iterations reached
- At k=16, the Truncate strategy on a 3B model achieves:
  - V* All: 89.53 (vs. 85.86 for majority voting)
  - V* Attr: 94.78 (vs. 92.17)
  - V* Pos: 81.57 (vs. 76.32)

---

### 3. Computational Cost at Inference Time

**Critical finding: The paper provides NO explicit computational cost analysis.** This is a significant gap.

Implicit cost indicators:
- Each iteration requires a full forward pass of Perceval (same size as policy: 3B or 7B) to detect errors
- Each iteration also requires regeneration by the policy model from the truncation point
- With k=16 iterations, worst case = 16 Perceval calls + 16 partial regenerations
- The authors note they "trade a bit more compute for stronger factual grounding" but never quantify this

**Estimated overhead (inferred):**
- Perceval is the same architecture/size as the policy model (Qwen2.5-VL 3B or 7B)
- Each verification step = ~1 full forward pass of an equivalent-size model
- For k iterations: overhead is approximately k * (cost of one PRM pass + cost of partial regeneration)
- This is substantially more expensive than majority voting (which only requires N independent generations)

No latency numbers, throughput benchmarks, or wall-clock comparisons are provided anywhere in the paper or in follow-up discussions found online.

### 4. Comparison to Lightweight Probe/MLP on Hidden States

**Perceval does NOT compare against probe-based approaches.** However, I found highly relevant work:

**HALP (arXiv 2603.05465, March 2026)** detects hallucinations in VLMs using hidden state probes:
- Architecture: 3-layer MLP (512 -> 256 -> 128 dimensions)
- Inference time: **10-15ms** per sample (vs. full model forward pass for Perceval)
- Overhead: **<1%** relative to full generation
- AUROC: ~0.89 average on query token representations
- Operates **pre-generation** (single forward pass, no decoding needed)

**Key differences:**
| Aspect | Perceval | HALP-style Probe |
|--------|----------|-----------------|
| Parameters | 3B-7B (full VLM) | ~200K (tiny MLP) |
| Inference cost | Full forward pass per check | 10-15ms per sample |
| Granularity | Token-span error grounding with explanations | Binary hallucination probability |
| Actionability | Can truncate and guide regeneration | Can only flag risk pre-generation |
| Training data | Requires carefully curated perception-centric annotations | Trained on hidden states from existing data |

The fundamental trade-off: Perceval is orders of magnitude more expensive but provides actionable, fine-grained error localization that enables the truncation-regeneration loop. Probes are nearly free but only provide a binary signal.
